title: Private Deployments 14 VPC & On-Prem Reference, Requirements, and Day-2 Ops
author: Priya Nair
summary: Comprehensive reference combining VPC and on-prem reference architectures, customer requirements library, on-prem packaging guidance, day-2 operations, and formal upgrade & rollback procedures for Redwood Private deployments.
content:
Overview:

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Private deployments covering VPC and on-prem reference architectures, customer requirements and checklist, packaging and installation guidance, day-2 operational procedures, and safe upgrade & rollback playbooks. It is intended for Solutions Engineers, Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), and customer engineering teams responsible for designing, installing, and operating Redwood in private environments.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Solutions Engineers, SREs, customer infra engineers, and implementation partners.
- Scope: Network, compute, storage, security, packaging, installation checklist, monitoring, backup & restore, upgrades, rollbacks, and common day-2 ops runbooks.

Goals:
- Provide repeatable reference architectures for VPC and on-prem installs.
- Capture customer requirements that trigger architecture choices and tradeoffs.
- Standardize day-2 operations (monitoring, incident triage, scaling, backups).
- Define deterministic upgrade and rollback procedures with validation steps and SLO checks.

Prerequisites and assumptions:
- Customer has signed a Redwood Private agreement and provided required network and compliance approvals.
- Access: Engineering contact(s) with admin privileges in target environment, KMS/HSM ownership if required.
- Inventory: list of target hosts, GPU types, network CIDRs, storage class definitions.

Reference architectures (high level):

1) VPC Deployment (recommended for cloud customers)
- Topology: Dedicated VPC, multiple private subnets (control & data plane separation), public subnet for bastion/NAT where required.
- Components:
  - Control plane (customer-managed or Redwood-managed control plane depending on contract) - runs API gateway, console, and orchestration components.
  - Inference pool (GPU nodes) - separated into model pools (e.g., small/latency, large/batch).
  - Storage: object storage (S3-compatible) for model artifacts and logs; block storage for persistent volumes (PVCs).
  - Networking: Private load balancers, security groups, NAT Gateways as required.
- Typical Sizing: 1-4 control-plane m5.large equiv; GPU fleet sized by expected qps and batch size. See sizing table below.

2) On-Prem (air-gapped or regulated)
- Topology: Customer data center with segregated management VLAN and inference VLANs. Optional DMZ for external integrations.
- Packaging: Container images delivered via air-gapped registry or pre-loaded tarballs; Helm charts with offline dependencies.
- Storage: NFS/CSI or local NVMe depending on performance needs; model artifacts stored on on-prem object store (MinIO) or local filesystem.
- Security: HSM/KMS integration via removable key transfer procedure; strict RBAC and audit logging to customer SIEM.

Sizing and performance guidance (example):
| Workload class | Example model | GPU per replica | Target latency (p50/p95) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Low-latency | small LLM (7B quant) | 1x A10G | 50ms / 250ms | Continuous batching disabled for lowest p50 |
| Mixed | 13B quant | 1x A100 80GB | 150ms / 700ms | Autoscale target: 10-20 qps per GPU |
| High-throughput | 70B model | 2x A100 80GB (tensor-split) | 300ms / 1.2s | Use batching + KV cache; prefer Dedicated |

Customer requirements library (summary of common asks):
- Networking: Required CIDRs, proxy / outbound restrictions, private endpoints, split DNS.
- Security & Compliance: KMS/HSM support, FIPS requirement, audit log retention window, customer-controlled access.
- Data residency: region constraints, on-prem storage, backup retention policies.
- Integrations: SIEM, IAM/SSO (SAML/OIDC), private registries.
- Capacity & SLAs: expected qps, per-model latency targets, peak concurrency, maintenance windows.
- Upgrade constraints: blackout windows, canary host lists, approval gating (legal/compliance).

Deployment checklists (VPC & on-prem):

A) Pre-deployment checklist (customer readiness)
1. Confirm contract and scope: confirm Dedicated vs Private, control plane ownership.
2. Network: validate VPC/subnets, route tables, NAT/IGW, required firewall openings (list below).
3. Identity: ensure SAML/OIDC config available or service accounts for automation.
4. Storage: provision object storage bucket and credentials (or MinIO endpoint).
5. Compute inventory: list of GPU hosts, CPU/memory, OS versions, drivers, and runtime (containerd/docker).
6. Security: KMS/HSM access and key policies documented.

B) Network/security ports (minimum required)
- Control plane -> Inference pool: TCP 443 (API), gRPC ports as configured (default 50051), health-check ports 8000.
- Admin bastion: SSH 22 from approved admin CIDRs (or SSM equivalent).
- Outbound: allow HTTPS to Redwood artifact registries (if not air gapped).

C) Packaging & install steps (on-prem air-gapped mode)
1. Validate host OS and GPU driver versions (NVIDIA driver >= 525.xx, CUDA >= 11.8 where required).
2. Install container runtime and pre-pull images via offline registry or provided tarballs.
3. Apply Helm charts with values.yaml adjusted for local registries, storage classes, and resource requests.
4. Run initial smoke tests: health endpoints, sample inference request, metrics scraping.

Day-2 operations (operational playbooks):

Monitoring & alerting baseline:
- Metrics to collect: per-model latency (p50/p95/p99), token/sec, GPU utilization, queue length, batch size, error-rate by route.
- Default alerts:
  - High error rate: >1% 5-minute error rate -> P1 paging to oncall.
  - Latency breach: p95 > SLO for 10m -> P2.
  - GPU OOM or node failure -> automated reprovisioning runbook.

Common runbooks (short form):
1) Instance failure (GPU node down)
  1. Identify failing node via node exporter / kube events.
  2. Drain node and check replicated pods scheduled elsewhere.
  3. If autoscaling enabled, verify scale-up. If not, provision replacement node and attach to cluster.
  4. After replacement, run model-warmup to populate KV cache if required.

2) High p95 latency for a specific model
  1. Check model route: recent config changes, concurrency settings, batching profile.
  2. Inspect queue lengths and batch sizes; increase pool size or adjust batching thresholds.
  3. If degradation persists, failover route to compatible lower-size model variant (configured in routing policy).

3) Log collection & triage
  - Collect: control-plane logs, inference pod logs, GPU driver syslogs, and relevant metrics window.
  - If customer SIEM onboarded, ensure events are pushed with correct tags (customer_id, deployment_id).

Backups and restores:
- Models: models should be stored in object storage with versioned bulbs. Periodic snapshots of model registry metadata are required.
- State: persistent postgres/metadata DB backups using scheduled snapshots layered with WAL shipping where possible.
- Restore validation: always perform a dry restore in a staging environment before production restores.

Upgrade and rollback procedures (formal playbook):

Principles:
- Always run canary upgrades on a small subset of hosts before rolling cluster-wide.
- Verify functional and perf smoke tests at each stage.
- Have a tested rollback artifact and clearly defined rollback trigger conditions.

Release gating checklist (pre-upgrade):
- Confirm backups for metadata and models exist and checksums match.
- Confirm maintenance window and stakeholders ACK.
- Confirm monitoring dashboards and synthetic test job configured.

Step-by-step upgrade (control plane):
1. Create release bundle and signature; store in customer artifact repo.
2. Deploy to canary namespace (1-2 control-plane replicas).
3. Run automated smoke tests (auth, basic inference, metrics ingestion).
4. If canary passes for 30-60 minutes, progressively roll to remaining control-plane nodes.
5. After control plane completes, proceed to inference pools in waves.
6. For each inference pool wave: drain, update daemonsets/deployments, run warmup jobs, verify latency and error rates.

Rollback procedure (if canary or wave fails):
1. Immediately stop rollout and mark the release as failed.
2. If control plane canary fails: restore previous control-plane pods from previous image and revalidate.
3. If inference pool wave fails: scale down new replicas and scale up previous image replicas.
4. Restore metadata DB from snapshot only if data corruption is suspected - otherwise prefer redeploy of previous container images.
5. Post-incident: create incident review and update the upgrade checklist.

Validation & acceptance criteria post-upgrade:
- Synthetic tests pass (latency, correctness) for 60 minutes.
- No more than 0.5% error rate over baseline for 30 minutes.
- GPU utilization and per-model latencies within expected ranges.

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team (oncall rotation).
- Escalation: Solutions Engineer -> SRE -> Applied ML -> Product Engineering.
- Contact: private-deployments-oncall@redwood.ai (alias).

Appendices:
A. Example values.yaml snippets (networking and storage overrides):
- network.externalLoadBalancer: false
- storage.model.bucket: "s3://customer-model-bucket"
- imageRegistry: "10.0.0.5:5000"

B. Common troubleshooting commands:
- kubectl get pods -n redwood 
- kubectl logs <pod> -n redwood --follow
- nvidia-smi (on host)

If additional customer-specific constraints exist (e.g., FIPS/HSM, extended data-retention, air-gapped requirements), use the Customer Requirements Checklist below as the canonical input for architecture selection.

Customer Requirements Checklist (copyable for pre-sales):
1. Is the deployment cloud (VPC) or on-prem (air-gapped)?
2. Expected concurrent QPS & peak concurrency windows.
3. Per-model latency targets (p50/p95).
4. Approved GPU SKUs and available inventory.
5. Storage options (S3, MinIO, NFS) and retention policies.
6. KMS/HSM requirements and approved vendors.
7. Compliance needs (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI, FIPS).
8. Integrations required (SIEM, SSO, private registries).
9. Maintenance window constraints and blackout periods.
10. Backup & restore RPO/RTO targets.
